_comment: Every place the release version is written. scripts/bump_version.sh writes
them and scripts/check_release_versions.sh reads them, so the two cannot
disagree about what a release touches. Adding a manifest without adding it
here fails tests/release/version-sites.test.sh, which derives the expected
set from the tree rather than trusting this list to be complete.
json_sites name JSON PATHS, not a count of matches. package-lock.json has
178 'version' fields and two of them are ours; counting matches would have
compared the release against every npm dependency.
Cargo.lock is under generated_lockfiles, never edited as text. A textual
substitution there rewrites any third-party crate sharing the version
string: on 2026-09-22 a global sed of 0.17.0 -> 0.18.0 turned hashbrown
0.17.0 into a version that does not exist at its recorded checksum, and the
rehearsal failed with 'cannot update the lock file'. cargo owns that file.
